rationale: The printed linkage rates match the frozen summaries: 66 of 1790 in data/lit/openalex-records-summary.json and 75 of 7572 in data/lit/openalex-frame-P01v2-summary.json, rates 3.7 and 1.0 percent. The server tables match those files. The 200 / 80 / below-80 rule is written before the probes, and the document correctly discloses that version change is not peer review. Those parts hold. The sample is not preprint and published pairs of meta-research articles. studies/_shared/openalex_probe.py counts any location whose display_name contains a preprint-server substring, including the primary location. Concatenating 66 and 75 gives 141 only by not deduplicating; the two OpenAlex files share 3 preprint-flagged PMIDs because frame-P01v2.jsonl still contains the 205 tier A overlaps P01v2 later excluded, so unique flagged PMIDs are 138. Of those, 33 are OpenAlex type preprint with no journal location, and 17 independent-frame records are Zenodo-only, including Dataset deposits. Unique works with both a journal location and a named-server location: 105. After dropping exact arXiv and SSRN: 69. The 33 / 108 exclusion does not recompute from the printed server counts (24+10+3=37) or from the frozen files (37 unique exact arXiv/SSRN articles). Probe PC is outstanding, so scorable n is unknown. The document's own rule sends n under 80 to the agenda. The reduced-form McNemar on preprint_critical by published_critical does not implement 'became less critical, unchanged as no,' and cannot see ordinal softening, which is the hypothesis and is the change Brierley et al. 2022 already coded on 184 bioRxiv/medRxiv pairs. The unscreened P01v2 frame is not a meta-research corpus. Calling 141 a preregistered secondary after seeing the counts, and making 'biomedical' servers the primary after a draft that tried to keep arXiv because 108 was 'below 80,' is not preregistration.

findings.problem: The unit is 'preprint and published version pairs of the same meta-research article.' The probe does not identify that unit. It flags a work if any OpenAlex location display_name contains biorxiv, medrxiv, arxiv, ssrn, osf, preprints.org, research square, zenodo, psyarxiv, or metarxiv. The comment says 'other than the primary,' but the loop never skips the primary location. Frozen consequence: of 138 unique flagged PMIDs, 33 are OpenAlex type preprint with no journal location (8 in tier A, 25 in the frame after removing tier A PMIDs), including PMID 41992899, a medRxiv record with no journal counterpart. Seventeen independent-frame records are Zenodo-only. PMID 37401199 (eLife) has raw_type Dataset at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10722193. PMID 32550247 is a Twitter chatter dataset whose primary location is PubMed. Those are not preprint-journal version pairs. The substring 'arxiv' also matches metarxiv and psyarxiv. A missed true pair may be missing at random; a Zenodo dataset or a preprint-only PubMed record counted as a pair is a false positive, and it is concentrated in the frame that supplies most of the 75.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Require a journal or publishedVersion location and a distinct preprint-server location that is not a data repository. Skip the primary location when it is the preprint. Drop OpenAlex type=preprint with no journal counterpart. Stop treating Zenodo, and any location with raw_type Dataset, as a preprint version. Re-run PA and PB under that rule and replace every pair count in this document.
findings.quote: Meta-research articles with both a preprint and a published version, identified from OpenAlex `locations` where a source is a named preprint server.

findings.problem: Reduced-protocol status is locked by 141 and 108. 141 is 66+75. The frozen OpenAlex files share 3 preprint-flagged PMIDs because the frame probe was run on all 7617 frame-P01v2 records, before the 205 tier A overlaps were removed, so unique flagged works are 138. Unique works with both a journal location and a named-server location: 105. Exact arXiv plus SSRN unique articles: 37, not 33; 141 minus 37 is 104, not 108; 138 minus 37 is 101. After that exclusion, journal-plus-server works are 69. Probe PC (both full texts retrievable) is still outstanding, so the n that can be scored is unknown and is the n the decision rule needs. Under the document's own thresholds, a true pair count under 80 is an agenda item, not a reduced protocol. The 3.7 and 1.0 percent rates are correctly 66/1790 and 75/7572 under the probe's definition; they are not rates of preprint-journal pairs.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Deduplicate the two frames by PMID before adding. Apply the tier A exclusion to the frame first. Count unique articles, not 66+75. Recompute the arXiv/SSRN cut from unique articles. Run PC. Apply the 200 / 80 / below-80 rule to the scorable pair count. If that n is under 80, reclassify the document as agenda.
findings.quote: arXiv and SSRN contribute 33 of the 141 pairs and are mostly science-of-science rather than biomedical meta-research. Excluding them leaves 108, still within the 80 to 200 band, so the primary analysis is restricted to biomedical preprint servers

findings.problem: Half the sample is the unscreened P01v2 qualified tier B frame (7572 OpenAlex matches from 7617 PMIDs). That frame was built to be screened because a subject-matter query returns trials, clinical reviews, and databases as well as meta-research. P06 never screens it. Frozen titles among the independent-frame 'pairs' include PMID 39011096, a sham-controlled photodynamic therapy trial; PMID 42282195, a platform clinical trial design; PMID 27199606, a butterfly distribution database; and PMID 34816577, a Mediterranean-diet review in children. Tier A is the only self-named meta-research corpus, and after dropping preprint-only records it has 58 journal-plus-server works, 24 of them arXiv. Pooling an unscreened frame with tier A does not produce 'meta-research articles.' Selection into preprint locations also differs by frame (3.7 percent versus 1.0 percent), so the combined 141 is not one sampling frame.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Do not call the P01v2 frame meta-research until it is screened with a rule frozen before conclusion scoring. Report tier A pairs separately. If a screened frame is used, publish the eligibility flow and the post-screen pair count, and only then apply the section 4 decision rule.
findings.quote: Meta-research articles with both a preprint and a published version, identified from OpenAlex `locations` where a source is a named preprint server.

findings.section: 2. Hypothesis; 5. Exposure and outcome; 6. Analysis, in the reduced form
findings.problem: The hypothesis is that the published conclusion is less critical than the preprint conclusion. Section 5 still scores a five-point scale from strongly critical to endorsing. Section 6 then says that scale is not used, and defines a binary 'became less critical, yes or no, with unchanged pairs retained as no.' The code is McNemar on preprint_critical by published_critical, which tests equal marginal rates of being critical, plus an exact binomial on discordant pairs, which ignores unchanged pairs. Those three estimands are not the same. Dichotomizing each version as critical or not also misses the hypothesized effect: a move from strongly critical to moderately critical is softening and is invisible to McNemar on two 'is critical' flags. That is the change the five-point scale was built to see, and it is the change most pairs will show if they change at all. No expected discordant count or detectable effect is computed, so the claim that 141 (or 108) supports a reduced protocol rather than an agenda item is unsupported even if the pair count were right.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Define one estimand. If it is net directional shift among pairs that change, use McNemar or an exact binomial on discordant pairs and delete 'unchanged pairs retained as no.' If it is any softening on the five-point scale, keep the ordinal score at this n and do not dichotomize each version. State the smallest shift that counts and compute power from an expected discordant rate before locking the reduced form.
findings.quote: The outcome is binary: did the concluding claim become less critical, yes or no, with unchanged pairs retained as "no".

findings.problem: The document presents preprint-versus-journal conclusion change as a gap this design can newly measure. It cites no prior work. Brierley et al. 2022 already compared 184 bioRxiv/medRxiv preprint-published pairs, coded abstract conclusion changes including softening, and asked whether conclusions change under peer review. Klein et al. 2019 measured preprint-to-published textual change. Carneiro et al. 2020 compared reporting quality in paired preprint and journal versions. Nicholson et al. 2022 measured linguistic shifts in about 18,000 pairs. Bero et al. and Oikonomidi et al. compared conclusions in COVID-19 clinical preprint-journal pairs. The unoriginal piece is the pair comparison and the softening code. What would be new, and is not yet shown to be feasible, is restricting that comparison to meta-research conclusions about research practice.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Add a related-work section that cites Brierley et al. 2022 (PLoS Biol 20:e3001285), Klein et al. 2019, Carneiro et al. 2020, and Nicholson et al. 2022. State what is new: restriction to meta-research conclusions about research practice, not the preprint-versus-journal comparison. Either reuse a published softening code or justify a different scale.
findings.quote: This is measurable because meta-research increasingly appears as a preprint first, and both versions persist.

findings.problem: The description and section 1 frame the study as whether peer review blunts criticism. Section 7 then says the design attributes nothing to review specifically, and 'What this cannot show' repeats that time, new data, and author revision are not separated from review. Those two claims cannot both stand as the question the document answers. A paired version contrast measures change between two public texts. It does not measure review. Marking the threat 'disclosed' does not make the title or section 1 true.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Change the title, description, and section 1 so the question is version change, which is what the design measures. Keep peer review as a mechanism this design cannot isolate. Do not use 'whether peer review blunts criticism' as the document's question.
findings.quote: the design attributes nothing to review specifically

findings.problem: The written decision rule chooses full versus reduced versus agenda from pair count. It does not choose the primary population. After seeing the counts, a first draft kept arXiv in the primary analysis by claiming 108 was below 80. The published text reverses that and calls the biomedical cut 'the primary analysis, not a subgroup' and calls the full 141 a 'preregistered secondary,' because 'both counts were known before either analysis was specified.' Knowing the counts before specifying which sample is primary is looking at the data, not preregistration. Agenda.qmd also states that nothing here is registered. The restriction is 'excluding arXiv and SSRN,' not restriction to biomedical preprint servers: OSF Preprints, Zenodo, Research Square, and PsyArXiv remain. Those are not biomedical servers.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Drop 'preregistered.' If biomedical servers are the population of interest, write that restriction into the decision rule without reference to whether 108 cleared 80. Name the servers that remain and justify each; do not call OSF, Zenodo, Research Square, or PsyArXiv biomedical preprint servers.
findings.quote: the full 141 pairs are reported as a preregistered secondary. Neither is a subgroup fished for after the fact: both counts were known before either analysis was specified, and both are published.

findings.problem: The outcome is the direction and strength of the concluding claim, taken from the abstract conclusion and the discussion, on a five-point scale that section 6 then discards. There is no coding rule for what 'critical of the practice it studied' means, no rule when abstract and discussion disagree, and no stated size for the author-labeled reference sample. Copying P03's kappa 0.70 gate does not supply those. P03 classifies one abstract per article into inadequate, adequate, mixed, or not applicable. This task is paired, version-blind, ordinal criticism. A model can pass overall kappa 0.70 while never detecting the ordinal softening the hypothesis cares about, especially after the reduced form collapses the scale. Version-blind presentation is necessary and does not stop journal copyediting, 'this journal' phrasing, or typesetting from identifying the published text.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Freeze a coding manual for the scale that will actually be analyzed, with examples and a rule when abstract and discussion disagree. State the reference-sample size before labeling. Validate that reduced-form label, not a five-point score that is then thrown away. Report class-specific agreement for softening versus no change versus hardening.
findings.quote: Scoring is by the same gated procedure as [P03](P03-bad-news-citation.qmd): the author labels a reference sample, two models label it blind, and the study does not proceed unless a model reaches kappa 0.70 against the author.

findings.section: 7. Threats, and what happened to each
findings.problem: Scorer knowledge of version is marked Removed. Stripping dates, venue, and version labels reduces the leak; it does not remove it. Journal copyediting, reference lists, and layout still identify the published version, which is the version the hypothesis says should be less critical.
findings.what_would_fix_it: Mark the threat as reduced, not removed, and add a post-scoring check of whether models can still pick the published text.
findings.quote: Scorer knows which version is which | Version-blinded presentation, randomized order, stripped metadata | Removed

findings.problem: data_source lists bioRxiv, medRxiv, and OSF. The probe and the server tables also use arXiv, SSRN, Research Square, Zenodo, PsyArXiv, and MetaRXiv. Readers who trust the YAML will not find the sample they think they are reading.
findings.what_would_fix_it: List every server the probe actually matches, or restrict the probe to the servers named in data_source.
findings.quote: data_source: "OpenAlex locations; bioRxiv, medRxiv and OSF preprint servers"
